To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the essential manifold, the objective function and the optimization technique are all important factors that influence the performance and robustness of motion and structure estimation algorithms.

the essential manifold, which has the same parameterization as the motion and structure space, is the only unknown parameter space in motion and structure recovery; the optimal triangulation procedure is the most natural objective function for this task; and the Riemannian geometry of the essential manifold is crucial for efficient computation and for the interpretation of the results.

(1) the optimization problem for motion and structure estimation is a Riemann optimization problem, (2) the objective function does not matter as long as the optimization algorithm is Riemannian and (3) the bas-relief ambiguity can only be resolved by a prior on the motion or the structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a unified treatment of various objective functions, optimization techniques, and sensitivity and robust problems.
a unified study of motion and structure estimation from multiple images.
the fundamental aspects of motion and shape recovery, including the choice of objective functions and optimization techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the choice of the objective function is important for the robustness of the estimation, the nonlinear optimization is essential for the sensitivity and the efficiency of the estimation.
the “epipolar constraints” is the most robust and reliable objective function, while the “triangulation” is the most sensitive and least reliable objective function.

the “epipolar constraints” and the “reprojection error minimization” are indeed equivalent in terms of the critical points, and the proposed Riemannian nonlinear optimization algorithm is the most effective in terms of the number of critical points and computational cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the presence of Gaussian noise, the proposed nonlinear optimization technique is robust and efficient, and that it is not necessary to consider the effect of basrelief ambiguity, rotation confounding, translation confounding or other types of local minimum when the noise level is below a certain threshold.
the proposed optimization techniques provide a unified framework for motion and structure recovery.
the proposed optimization techniques provide a unified framework to address the motion and structure problem, which is robust against noise and outliers and is computationally efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sensitivity and robustness properties of a technique can be understood in terms of the geometry of the essential manifold, which is independent of the choice of objective functions and optimization techniques.
a unified geometric approach to motion and structure recovery provides a clear account of the existing techniques and leads to a new understanding of the sensitivity and robustness problems.
the choice of the objective function and the optimization technique are not independent and should be carefully matched to achieve the best performance.
